newsitem.title: BRAZIL: IMF official says concerned about Brazil debt.
newsitem.headline: IMF official says concerned about Brazil debt.

text.p: Brazil must take steps to avoid significant growth in its debt to Gross Domestic Product ratio, said Vitor Tanzi, fiscal affairs director of International Monetary Fund (IMF).

Tanzi said Brazil's current interest rate levels combined with a primary surplus of only 1.0 percent and economic growth of 3.0-4.0 percent annually would cause "quite substantial growth" in the ratio.
"This is something that cannot be ignored. It must be dealt with as early as possible," he told an International Seminar on Public Finances in the Brazilian capital Brasilia.
Tanzi also said the results of an IMF study on Brazil's debt were "worrisome" and he stressed the need for a higher primary surplus.
Brazil's net public sector debt to GDP ratio currently stands at about 32 percent.
Tanzi declined to reveal the exact results of the IMF study on Brazil's debt to GDP ratio.
"I can tell you, it would be quite substantial growth," he said. "If you don't have (structural) adjustment today, the ratio of debt to GDP will grow very fast."

Tanzi acknowledged that Brazil's debt to GDP ratio was not high compared with other countries but he said, "What's worrying us are the dynamics of the 32 percent when real interest rates are very high."
